newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Chile, Bolivia in Brazil Mercosur import deal.
newsitem.headline: Chile, Bolivia in Brazil Mercosur import deal.

text.p: Mercosur free trade associates Bolivia and Chile are included in a deal that Brazil struck with the trade bloc over controversial new import financing rules, said Gustavo Franco, International Affairs director of Brazilian Central Bank.

Franco said that Uruguay, though a member of Mercosur, was effectively left out of the agreement because it was not a signatory of a convention on settling trade disputes under the ALADI Latin American free trade agreement.
"This applies to Mercosur including Chile and Bolivia," Franco said.

Franco said the deal was struck Wednesday with visiting Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez and exempts Mercosur imports from new short-term financing restrictions if they are worth less than $40,000 and backed by so-called CCR reciprocal trade credits.
Franco said Uruguay had not found a convention on trade dispute solutions under which CCRs were established.
Asked if Uruguay was therefore effectively left out of the deal, Franco said, "Yes".

On Wednesday, Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan had suggested that Chile and Bolivia, which have signed associate free trade agreements with the bloc, would not immediately be included and that talks would be held with them.
In a decree to be published Friday, the Brazilian Central Bank says the partial exemptions from the import financing restrictions will only apply to "members of Mercosur."
